title: The Kiprun Singapore 2026: Decathlon's High-Speed Debut in Kallang
seo_title: Kiprun Singapore 2026 Review: Decathlon's New Half
meta_description: Decathlon and MetaSport launch The Kiprun Singapore 2026, a Sept 27 half marathon in Kallang with festival energy and budget-friendly pricing.
dek: Decathlon's performance running label makes its Singapore racing debut with a Kallang-based half marathon promising fast, turn-light roads, festival flair and unusually low entry fees.
verdict: The Kiprun Singapore 2026 is Decathlon and MetaSport's bet that a half marathon can be both technically serious and genuinely fun. Expect a rhythm-friendly course with wide roads, minimal turns, 5km splits and wave starts anchored near Kallang and Marina Bay, four distances from a 670m Kids Dash to the flagship 21.1km, and unusually low entry pricing for Singapore. As an inaugural event it carries first-edition risk, but the organiser's pedigree and pricing make it worth a look for PB-chasers and first-timers alike.

sections.heading: The Course: A Fast, Wide-Road Half Marathon by Design
paragraphs: Decathlon and MetaSport have pitched the flagship 21.1km as a race engineered for rhythm rather than survival, with the course designed to prioritise wide roads and minimal turns so runners can settle into pace early and hold it to the finish [3]. Structured wave starts are also part of the plan, intended to cut early congestion and give faster "performance wave" runners clear road from the gun [3].

To back the pacing promise, organisers say the route will carry accurate timing splits at every 5km alongside experienced pacers, useful markers for anyone chasing a specific split or a first sub-2-hour half [3]. The full route has not been published, but Decathlon's own teaser imagery of Marina Bay Sands, Gardens by the Bay and the Singapore Flyer points toward the Marina Bay waterfront corridor that hosts many of Singapore's biggest road races [4].

sections.heading: Distances and Who It's For
paragraphs: Four distances run under one banner: the headline 21.1km half marathon, a 10km, a 5km and a 670m Kids Dash, giving families and first-timers an on-ramp alongside the serious half-marathon field [1][5]. Podium prizes are on offer for the top finishers in the half marathon, 10km and 5km categories, a sign MetaSport wants a real competitive edge behind the festival branding [5].

sections.heading: Logistics, Pricing and the Decathlon Angle
paragraphs: The event sits on Decathlon Singapore's home turf at the Decathlon Singapore Lab in Kallang, near the National Stadium, running across a long race-day window from 4am to 2pm to accommodate bump-in, multiple wave starts and the post-race village [3][5]. Decathlon is leaning hard on value, launching Super Early Bird pricing from S$78 for the half marathon, S$60 for the 10km and S$10 for the Kids Dash, positioned as one of the more affordable half-marathon entries in the Singapore market [6].

This isn't Decathlon's first attempt at mass-participation running in Singapore — the brand ran events in 2017 and 2019 and staged the Decathlon Run as recently as 2022 before shifting to virtual formats during the pandemic — so there's some institutional memory behind the operation, even if the Kiprun-branded format itself is brand new [5]. Local reaction has been warm: Singapore Runners Club founder Eugene Beh welcomed Decathlon's return with a competitive run as good news for the community [4].

sections.heading: Atmosphere: "Elite Logistics, Festival Energy"
paragraphs: The organisers' own framing for the event is built around closing the gap between a technically rigorous timed race and a fun run with entertainment bolted on the side, addressing rising costs and inconsistent race-day standards runners have complained about elsewhere [6]. Concretely that translates into entertainment zones, live music and activations woven into the route and the start/finish precinct at the Decathlon Lab [1][2].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: Because this is the inaugural edition, there's no finish-line data or crowd-sourced race report to lean on yet — everything here is the organisers' stated intent rather than a proven track record, which is worth weighing before you commit training weeks to it [5]. That said, the ingredients on paper are sound: a pacing-friendly course design, 5km splits, wave starts, competitive pricing and an organiser with existing experience running Singapore participation events [2][3][6].

If you're chasing a half-marathon PB on a course meant to be turn-light and rhythm-friendly, or you want a lower-cost September half with a family-friendly Kids Dash attached, Kiprun Singapore is a reasonable bet — just treat it as a first edition and build in some tolerance for opening-year kinks [1][3].

faqs.question: When and where is the Kiprun Singapore 2026?
faqs.answer: It takes place on Sunday, 27 September 2026 at the Decathlon Singapore Lab in Kallang, near the National Stadium, with the event day running from roughly 4am to 2pm to cover multiple waves and the festival village.

faqs.question: How much does the Kiprun Singapore cost?
faqs.answer: Super Early Bird pricing launched from S$78 for the 21.1km half marathon, S$60 for the 10km and S$10 for the Kids Dash, with organisers marketing it as one of the more affordable half-marathon entries in Singapore.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at Kiprun Singapore?
faqs.answer: There are four categories: a headline 21.1km half marathon, a 10km run, a 5km run, and a 670m Kids Dash aimed at younger participants, so families can join alongside serious half-marathon entrants.

faqs.question: Is this Decathlon's first running event in Singapore?
faqs.answer: It's the first Kiprun-branded race here, though Decathlon previously organised running events in 2017 and 2019 and last staged the Decathlon Run in 2022, giving this new MetaSport-run edition some operational history to draw on.
